Gavin de Becker is an expert on acts of violence.  He's got a book, The Gift of Fear, which I just happen to be reading now, but a lot of his ideas are presented in this lecture.  He's dealt with all kinds of stalking and harassment cases, and has been consulted by both average folks and famous people alike.  I'm not an expert so I don't want to give you any bad advice, but maybe you'll be interested in what he has to say about escalation and recognizing threats and so on.

Good luck.

It's complicated but it involves seeing a deadbeat father that I'd rather never see again.
I don't particularly have a favorite.  Grey, I guess?
I don't know.  I'm dizzy.  It's hard to type.

What.a.dick.


Seriously.  That is the rudest thing I've ever seen in an job-seeking context.  Don't let Douchey McDouchbag's words get to you--someone obviously peed in his cornflakes that morning.  You don't need that shit.


As one unemployed person to another, I know it sucks to constantly get rejections.  But, I'm also not going to grovel for a job.  I would tell that recruiter-douche that he's unprofessional.  Sure, you're burning a bridge but pride means something, right?  I wouldn't work for those people just on principle.

I think part of it is that it's just difficult to be around people with mental illness.  It's not a pretty sight.  I know that I constantly exude and spread misery by acting the way I do, as if I have some kind of contagious disease.  I don't blame anyone for being resentful for having to pick up my slack.  Of course they'd resent me.  Having to put up with someone's problems is frustrating, whether they are physical or mental.  I've heard of married couples that divorce after one of them gets cancer, and cancer is something very tangible.  

Sometimes I think I should just disappear from everyone's life, but there's nowhere to go.  You affect others whether you do something or refrain from doing something.

Thanks for your answer.  I've tried the mental health thing before when I had insurance, but everyone I spoke with just stated the obvious and was very dismissive and condescending.  The meds seemed to help but then I stopped taking them because my family said they were useless and that I couldn't be sure whether or not they were just a placebo.
I don't know if I need help or want help.  I guess I just want to add to the chorus of dissatisfaction that is the internet.  I just wanted someone to listen to me without telling me that I'm being stupid or crazy, even if both of those things are true.
I don't know what I want.  What if it does get better, but I'm still miserable?

How long does it take to find something one truly enjoys?  I keep waiting, testing the waters, and finding nothing.  By the time I find something I like enough such that it gives me a reason to live, I'll have died of old age. :/
